findings.text: Main allocation dispatch first consults per cpu cache when order qualifies and otherwise uses buddy path, then clears boosted watermark state and requests background reclaim when needed, and validates result range.

Buddy allocator acquires zone serialization, prefers high atomic reserve when requested, otherwise follows normal fallback chain with opportunistic high atomic use under shortage, retries tainted results, optionally grows reserve, and records allocation and locality counters.

Per cpu allocation serves from cached list and refills it in computed batches through bulk buddy path, diverting high atomic requests back to buddy path so reserves can form, and discards failed pages.
Page splitting warns on unexpected compound or uncounted state, marks trailing subpages as referenced, and propagates split through owner tag and memory cgroup accounting helpers.
Per cpu draining helpers reduce cached occupancy toward target high level in batch steps, either for one zone cache or for current processor across one or all zones.

Background reclaim wakeup ignores unmanaged or disallowed zones, raises node wide desired zone scope and order, suppresses wake when nobody waits or node already balanced without boost, optionally nudges compaction, otherwise wakes reclaim thread.

Fallback mode progresses from direct match to CMA area to whole block claim to fragmenting steal, with success in claim returning to direct mode while CMA and steal persist for later bulk iterations under same lock.

Cached high level decays gradually toward configured minimum by at most one eighth per pass bounded below by current occupancy minus scaled batch, signalling further work while above minimum or while draining.
High atomic capacity grows on precarious minimum watermark allocations and shrinks through zonelist ordered unreserve that converts one block at a time to requester kind until pressure eases.

Claim scans from largest block downward and only takes whole blocks of another mobility kind, honouring a block sized floor for small antifragment requests, while steal scans upward from requested size and expands a larger block even at fragmentation cost.
Movable allocations favour CMA area first when that area holds majority of spare capacity, and otherwise probe CMA area only after direct freelist fails, keeping regular and CMA usage balanced.

Antifragment requests never enter steal path and for sub block sizes never claim below block granularity, forcing retry through other zones without antifragment allowance when local freelists lack suitable blocks.

Refill size adapts to demand by clamping cached high level within configured bounds, growing high when zone healthy, doubling order zero batch on repeated allocation without free up to configured scale limit, and shrinking batch with order while keeping a small minimum.

High atomic reserve only forms on sufficiently large zones up to about one percent of managed memory aligned to block size, only from mergeable mobility kinds, and unreserve preserves at least one block unless forced while converting freed blocks to caller mobility kind.

Watermark check uses a cheap order zero usable free comparison against mark plus low memory reserve, falls back to full check, and for boosted high priority order zero minimum checks retries against unboosted minimum so reclaim wakes appropriately.

Allocation locality accounting distinguishes local versus remote node and hit versus miss plus foreign by comparing allocation zone node against current node and preferred zone node, and can be disabled through a static key.
Reclaim permission either compares inter node distance against a tunable threshold or unconditionally allows, depending on build variant.

Fragmentation avoidance derives from defragmentation mode, from reclaim allowance in allocation flags, and on certain builds from normal zone placement with populated successor, while CMA allowance derives only from movable mobility kind.
Boost detection scans zones from high to low ignoring unmanaged zones and reports boosted if any boost counter set, and wakeup suppresses reclaim wake when node balanced and no boost present.
Bulk removal appends pages in physical order to caller list tail, aiding merge friendly device access under suitable conditions.

Bulk and single buddy paths hold zone interrupt saving spin serialization across freelist search and removal, with a non blocking variant that attempts acquisition once and reports empty on contention.

Per cpu cache access uses dedicated per cpu spin serialization around list refill accounting and bulk release, with allocation using a try acquisition that yields to concurrent drain or interrupt reentry by returning empty.
High atomic reserve growth and release recheck limits and perform block conversion while holding zone interrupt saving serialization, tolerating racy pre checks outside the lock.
Buddy and per cpu paths loop on failed freshness validation of returned pages, so a persistently bad page could spin under repeated lock acquire and release cycles.

Accounting guards against reserve underflow when per cpu drain races unreserve and against oversized reserve estimates, and reserve sizing reads managed page count without lock before confirming under lock.
Non blocking callers receive immediate failure when zone or per cpu lock busy, requiring caller fallback rather than waiting.

Observed organization groups per order freelists in zone alongside lock and reserve and boost counters, per cpu caches with high bounds and batch and count plus per mobility order lists, and node control with desired reclaim scope and order and wait queue.
Fallback mode enumeration defines four ordered members for direct, CMA, claim and steal paths.
Node reclaim distance tunable defaults to configured distance constant.
